office_does: The county clerk is clerk of the Superior Court, keeping its case records and running jury administration, the family-law facilitator program and passport processing.
race_blurb: A rematch of 2022, when Republican Marty Young beat independent Sandra Arechiga by under 500 votes. Arechiga, a 12-year Clerk's Office employee who calls the office nonpartisan, led the August primary; Young runs on his first term and his management background.

candidates.summary: Family-law court facilitator and former jury administrator with 12 years in the Clerk's Office, running as an independent who says the office 'is not about party politics.'
highlights: Twelve years in the Clerk's Office, including six as Jury Administrator; now a Family Law Court Facilitator [S1]
Pledges transparency, bilingual service and 'working in good faith with Chelan County Commissioners' [S8]
Endorsed by retired Judge Chip Small, former Commissioner Bob Bugert and former Superior Court Commissioner Bart Vandegrift [S9]
Led the August primary with 8,553 votes (37.99%) [S4]

experience.basis: Non-incumbent who has never held elected office and is challenging the incumbent, though she argues from 12 years of work inside the office.

candidates.summary: Chelan County Clerk since his 2022 election, a former operations manager with an MBA and an engineering degree, and a Republican precinct committee officer.
highlights: Elected clerk in 2022, 16,456 to 15,978 over Arechiga [S5]
Cites court-record confidentiality, retention standards, grant processing and monthly quality-control reports [S1]
Led the office through a backlog of more than 6,000 filings after the 2026 county malware outage [S8]
Campaigns on 'common-sense conservative experience & retained knowledge' [S9]

experience.basis: One-term elected incumbent who asks to be re-elected on his record and 'retained knowledge'; his tenure is a single term.
